name: Mexican Plum

facts.where: Woodland edges, fence rows, creek banks

caution: Eat the flesh, never the cracked pits: like all wild cherries and plums the seeds carry cyanide-forming compounds. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: A single small tree can hang heavy with tart, thin-skinned plums. Pick the softest, darkest fruit; the tree fruits unevenly, so come back over a couple of weeks.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Tart and a little wild, Mexican plums make a jam or jelly with far more character than a grocery plum. Cook, strain, and sweeten.
